title: Band-9 Samples: How often do you watch programmes or read articles about wild animals? [Why?]
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 13 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 2 Test 4 question: “How often do you watch programmes or read articles about wild animals? [Why?]” Sample 1: Frequently Female Male I regularly tune in to shows and peruse articles about wildlife, as I find them incredibly fascinating. The reason behind my keen interest is that these programs and articles offer valuable insights into the diverse world of animals, their behaviors, and the ecosystems they inhabit. Moreover, they contribute to my understanding of the importance of conserving our natural world and its inhabitants. Sample 2: Frequently Female Male I frequently watch documentaries and read publications about wild creatures, as I am captivated by the remarkable diversity of species and their unique adaptations. The wealth of knowledge that these sources provide about the animal kingdom and their survival strategies in various habitats piques my curiosity and encourages me to learn more about the natural world. Sample 3: Frequently Female Male I find myself drawn to wildlife documentaries and articles fairly frequently, I’d say about 2-3 times a week. This interest stems from my fascination with the stunning diversity and complexity of life on our planet. It’s an opportunity not just to admire nature’s beauty, but also to understand the intricate balance that sustains various ecosystems. It’s like a jigsaw puzzle where each species has a crucial role, and learning about them helps me appreciate our interconnectivity. Sample 4: Moderately Female Male Well, I wouldn’t exactly describe myself as a fervent wildlife enthusiast, but I do indulge in such programmes or literature every now and then. It’s not an everyday occurrence, but maybe twice a week. The allure for me lies in the fact that these mediums offer a glimpse into the untouched corners of nature, a realm so intriguingly different from human society. Sample 5: Moderately Female Male Every now and then, I enjoy watching shows or perusing articles about untamed animals. My interest stems from the desire to learn more about their behavior, habitats, and the challenges they face. This knowledge inspires me to be more environmentally conscious and appreciate the beauty of the natural world. Sample 6: Rarely Female Male Honestly, I seldom find myself tuning into shows or perusing articles that focus on wildlife. The primary reason is that my schedule is typically chock-full with work commitments and personal pursuits. So, I prioritize content that directly pertains to my professional growth or hobbies, leaving little room for explorations into the realm of wild animals. Sample 7: Rarely Female Male To be honest, I don’t often indulge in wildlife programmes or articles. It’s not that I don’t appreciate the natural world, but my interests lie more in technology and artificial intelligence. However, when I do stumble upon a wildlife documentary, I find it oddly refreshing. The rawness of nature and the survival instincts of wild animals provide a stark contrast to our human-centric worldviews, which can be quite enlightening. Sample 8: Rarely Female Male Although I have a deep appreciation for the natural world, I seldom find myself immersed in documentaries or reading material about wildlife. The principal reason behind this infrequency is the lack of stimulation they provide to me personally. Despite the undeniable importance of these creatures in our ecosystem, the pacing and narrative style of these resources often leave me feeling disengaged. Sample 9: Never Female Male Frankly speaking, wildlife-related content – whether it’s on the television screen or printed on pages – has never managed to pique my interest. I tend to gravitate towards areas that delve into technological advancements and artificial intelligence. These fields, I believe, are pushing the boundaries of our collective knowledge and shaping our future. Thus, wildlife, though undeniably important, does not find a place in my usual media consumption. Sample 10: Never Female Male Living in the heart of a bustling city, I’ve always been more in tune with urban life and its dynamics. My interest tends to lean more towards architecture, urban planning, and societal issues. For some reason, wild animals and their habitats have never made it onto my radar. I suppose it’s because they feel rather distant from my everyday experiences.
